Well structured, well explained.
There is no doubt Bank nifty is in deep value, With exploding Energy prices and it's inflation RBI will be closer to hiking interest rates than feeding the growth engines. The Asset quality will show through when Borrowing costs increase, there is more likely hood of GNPA and NPA and we need to watch the direction of provisioning this Q2. That will be a headwind for all bankers, however this is when quality management process comes through, we are likely to see those with pristine asset quality run away with Investor interest, and in that space the Pvt biggies will do exceedingly well. ICICI has the best of book on Asset quality, HDFC   knowingly was going slow on its lending side or Asset side due to already mentioned extremely high CDR ratio. The coming in of FCNR deposits frees up pressure on CDR and releases the built up pipeline on the Asset side. The mgmt commentary every quarter was highlighting their conservativeness in lending. When the credit cycle reverses with higher interest rates those banks and managements who chased earnings  with loose lending, without quality will be the ones to pay a heavy price on deteriorating Asset quality. Another aspect that has spooked banking investors is the Insurance consult paper, this has put the spot light on insurance distributors or  fee dependent banks, smaller ones like IDFC will find this a tough period to navigate, as the possible lower fee income and unchecked lending in lower interest rates regimes will result in weakening Asset quality and distort all key ratios be it CDR, NIM, GNPA and NPA.
The sector valuations are attractive no doubt but we need to cherry pick the better Risk managed or Asset quality Franchises and for that Q2 earnings is the key, the question is would you rather invest in one having a higher NIM but deteriorating book? Or a lowering NIM but a improving Asset quality.
